resources.string: A keyboard that predicts on your phone and nowhere else.
Private field: no suggestions, nothing learned
Android asks you to allow any new keyboard in system settings.
Pick LocalType from the keyboard chooser. Long-press the space bar to switch back any time.

What you type stays on this phone. Suggestions, learning and the language model run here. LocalType goes online when you request an optional model download from Hugging Face, when you tap Check for updates, and when settings looks for a new version on its own (turn that off under About). None of these sends your typing. Google’s ML Kit library, which connects to Gemini Nano, can send Google statistics about that feature’s use.

LocalType privately stores words you add, learned word pairs, recent model suggestions, recent emoji and site names from web or email addresses you typed in full. It never saves the rest of an address. It also learns each letter key’s average finger-lift offset from known words completed without correction. These offsets help choose corrections; they never change which letter a tap types. Forget learned words clears them too.

Saved text stays in a private file excluded from backups and phone-to-phone transfers. Recent copies stay in memory for at most an hour. Copies marked sensitive, or made in password or incognito fields, are never kept. Unconfirmed misspellings are not learned. Password fields get no suggestions; incognito fields save nothing you type.

The optional typing log records suggestions and the words you type or tap next. It stays on this phone unless you export it. Turning logging off keeps the existing file; Clear log and Forget learned words remove it.

Fixes clear typos when you press Space or punctuation, using where your finger landed. Press Delete right after a fix to restore your spelling. Open Small typing fixes below for spacing and grammar help.

Right away, while Fix typos as I type is on: a fresh space before a comma, ! or ? is removed, a space before ) is removed only in a simple parenthesis you just typed, and a sentence starting “its been” becomes “it’s been”.

After the following word is complete, a few more spacing fixes can happen: “( hello” becomes “(hello”, “note : bring” becomes “note: bring”, and “Really?Yes” becomes “Really? Yes”, which requires a capitalized second word. Short labels, punctuation runs and emoticons stay as typed.

Less certain fixes wait for Apply: “its a”, “your not”, a repeated “the the”, capitals such as “WOrking”, a missing space in “hello,friend”, or a listed a/an phrase such as “a apple”.

To undo, press Delete immediately after an automatic fix, or tap Undo while it is shown. Undo keeps the text you typed afterward. These English prose fixes leave pasted or revisited text, address bars and private fields alone. Hashtags, @handles, paths and identifier spellings are protected.
Fix typos in web text boxes

Fixes clear typos in ordinary browser text boxes, including ones with autofill turned off. Passwords, URLs, email addresses, names and addresses keep their spelling. Takes effect in the next field you open.

Turns on Shift at the start of a sentence where the app asks for capitals, starts suggestions there with a capital, and makes a lone “i” into “I”. Turn it off to type in lowercase; Shift and caps lock still work. Takes effect in the next field you open.

Offers a fitting emoji in the last suggestion slot, like ☕ after “coffee” or 👍 after “thumbs up”. Tap it to swap the words for the emoji (delete right after brings them back), or hold for related emoji.

Suggests next words and completes words as you type. Chime is built in (about 2 MB, no download) and runs on this phone without saving your text or training on it. It starts on and remembers your choice; turned off, dictionary and learned-word suggestions remain. Changes take effect in the next ordinary text field. Everyday typing checks are still ongoing.

Type a web or email address in full to remember its site name, such as example.com. The rest of the address is never kept. After you type the site twice, starting it again offers a completion, including in browser address bars.\n\nNothing is kept or offered in password or incognito fields. Forget learned words removes remembered sites. Changes take effect in the next field.

resources.string: Forget learned words clears learned pairs, personal context, added words, remembered sites, learned tap offsets, the typing log and recent emoji. Saved text and skin-tone choices stay.
A spelling you deliberately keep or a suggestion you choose can appear after one use. Ordinary known words need two uses. Only words completed on this keyboard supply the preceding context.
Learned words and typing log cleared

Off unless you turn it on. The log helps me measure how well suggestions work. It records the suggestions, the word you type or tap next, and the words you typed before it in that sentence.

Only words typed or tapped on this keyboard in fields that allow logging are recorded. Passwords, incognito fields, address bars, pasted text and text already in the field are skipped. The file stays on this phone unless you export it.

Turning this off stops logging at the next field and keeps the existing file. Clear log and Forget learned words remove it.

string-array.name: tips_typing
string-array.item: Hold K or L for parentheses|Turn on Common symbols on hold under Keys and gestures. Slide in the same popup for accents and IPA.
Hold a letter|Its accents and IPA symbols open above it. Slide to the one you want, or lift on the first.
Hold a key in the top row|Types its number, while the number row is off.
Hold the period|Offers ? ! , ; : … and quotes.
Hold the comma|Offers an apostrophe, quotes, a dash, @ and &.
Double-tap Shift|Caps lock. Tap it again to turn it off. With TalkBack, hold Shift instead.
Tap space twice|Ends the sentence with a period and a space.
Slide through a word’s letters|Types the word, with Swipe typing turned on under Keys and gestures. It’s still experimental.

string-array.name: tips_editing
string-array.item: Slide along the space bar|Moves the cursor, one character at a time.
Slide left from Delete|Removes whole words. The strip shows what will go; slide back to keep it.
Hold Delete|Keeps deleting until you lift.
Press Delete right after a correction|Puts back what you typed.
Swipe two fingers across the keys|Runs the action set for that direction, with Two-finger swipes turned on under Keys and gestures.

string-array.name: tips_suggestions
string-array.item: Tap a word in quotes|Keeps your spelling, and stops it being corrected.
Tap the sparkle at the left of the strip|Asks Gemini Nano or Gemma for words, once one is set up under Suggestions.
Hold the sparkle|Proofreads the sentence you’re in.
Select a sentence|Tap Proofread selection in the strip.

string-array.name: tips_saved
string-array.item: Copy something|A clipboard icon at the left of the strip pastes it, for two minutes.
Hold the clipboard icon|Keeps what you copied in Saved text.
Tap the arrow at the right of the strip, then the clipboard|Opens Saved text: what you kept, and what you copied in the last hour.
Give a saved text a shortcut word|Under Saved text in settings. Type the word, then tap the text when it’s offered.
Start typing a site you’ve typed in full before|Tap it in the strip to finish the address.

string-array.name: tips_more
string-array.item: Tap the arrow at the right of the strip|Opens the tools row: clipboard, emoji, voice, undo and More. Tap the arrow again, or any key, to close it.
Hold the arrow at the right of the strip|Opens every tool over the keys, the same as More.
Hold a tool in the Tools panel|Adds it to the tools row, at the end, or takes it out. Keys and gestures in Settings resets it.
Tap the face in the tools row|Opens emoji. Search them by name from the panel.
Hold an emoji in the panel|Chooses its skin tone.
Tap the microphone in the tools row|Dictates. Tap the microphone in the strip, or any key, to stop.
Hold space|Opens the keyboard chooser. With another language turned on under Languages, it switches between them.
With TalkBack, focus the space bar|Its actions move the cursor and run your two-finger swipe actions.
An app won’t accept the keyboard|Some banking apps allow only the phone’s own keyboard. Switch with the keyboard button at the bottom of the screen while you use that app, then switch back.

resources.string: LocalType %1$s is out. Install it over this version to keep your words and settings.

When you open settings, at most every six hours, LocalType reads the version number on its download page and shows a banner at the top if a newer one is out. Nothing you type or set is sent, and the keyboard itself never checks.
Keeps 1 to 0 above the letters. Hold a number for its symbol, like ! on 1 or @ on 2.

A light buzz when you press or hold a key, slide along space or delete, or tap in the emoji and Saved text panels. While on, it follows your phone’s own touch vibration setting, so if that is off nothing vibrates.

Adds Spanish, with its own ñ key and the accents first on a hold of each vowel. Hold Space to switch; the space bar shows the language you’re typing. This is an early test: the Spanish word lists come from film subtitles and haven’t been checked by a native speaker, so some suggestions and corrections will be off. Slurs are left out, and swear words follow Suggest swear words. Spanish words are learned apart from English ones. Chime, the extra models, proofreading, swipe typing and the typing log stay English only.

Adds Portuguese, Brazilian spelling first, laid out as Android’s Portuguese keyboard is: hold c for ç, and hold a vowel for its accents. Hold Space to switch; the space bar shows the language you’re typing. This is an early test: the Portuguese word lists come from film subtitles and haven’t been checked by a native speaker, so some suggestions and corrections will be off. Slurs are left out, and swear words follow Suggest swear words. Portuguese words are learned apart from the other languages. Chime, the extra models, proofreading, swipe typing and the typing log stay English only.

Adds Hebrew, in the Israeli standard layout: eight letters and delete on the top row, ten on the home row and nine below, with no Shift since Hebrew has no capitals. Hold Space to switch; the space bar shows the language you’re typing. This is an early test: the Hebrew word lists come from film subtitles and haven’t been checked by a native speaker, so some suggestions and corrections will be off, and there is no next-word model yet, so suggestions come from the list and from what you type. Slurs are left out, and swear words follow Suggest swear words. Hebrew words are learned apart from the other languages. Chime, the extra models, proofreading, swipe typing and the typing log stay English only.

Adds a keyboard for phonetic transcription: hold Space to switch to it. A row of the commonest IPA symbols sits above the letters, and holding a letter offers the symbols related to it, like ŋ on n or ʃ on s. The comma key types the stress mark ˈ, with the other marks and diacritics on its hold, and the period key’s hold has ː and the brackets. Nothing is suggested, corrected, capitalized or learned while it’s on.
Swipe typing is English only for now
A keyboard that keeps your typing on this phone. Chime suggests words automatically, with no model download or account needed. First, enable LocalType and choose it as your keyboard.

Open Android’s keyboard settings and turn on LocalType. Android shows its standard warning for all keyboards. LocalType processes what you type on this phone; typing never uses the network. Come back here after enabling it.
LocalType is selected. Tap the field below and try “See you at” followed by a space. The strip offers words as you type. Tap a suggestion to insert it, or keep typing your own.
Autocorrect is separate from word suggestions. Press Delete right after a correction to restore your spelling. You can continue without typing a sample.

Chime suggests words as you type. It starts on; you can turn it off below or in Settings.\n\nThe sparkle button asks optional Gemini Nano or Gemma for other suggestions. Select a sentence and tap Proofread selection, or hold the sparkle to check the current sentence. Chime itself does not rewrite sentences.

The Chime model does not save your text or train on it. The keyboard can remember word pairs and tap offsets locally; Forget learned words clears them. Password and incognito fields teach nothing. The typing log stays off unless you turn it on. Nothing you type is uploaded.

Wider narrows ?123 and Return to make the space bar half a key wider. Widest also takes away the comma key, so the space bar is a key and a half wider; hold the period for a comma. Email and web address fields keep their @, / and .com keys. Takes effect in the next field you open.

For a tremor or limited reach. Each one is off until you choose it, and takes effect in the next field you open.
A touch that lands this soon after your last lift is ignored, and so is a second finger while one is already down, so a bounce or a brushing palm types nothing. Holding Shift turns caps lock on.

A key types only after your finger has stayed on it this long, then types when you lift. A bar fills along the key and it buzzes once it’s ready; lift sooner, or slide to another key, and nothing is typed there. Delete starts when it’s ready. Holding Shift turns caps lock on.

Keep your finger down and glide: resting on a key this long types it. Lifting types nothing, so to type a letter twice, move off it and back. Rest on Shift twice as long for caps lock. While this is on, swipe typing, slides, two-finger swipes, accent holds and the hold time above are off.
Keep a key until your finger clearly leaves
Once your finger is on a key, small movements don’t hand it to the next key: it has to travel about a third of a key past the edge first. Helps when a finger shakes or rolls before it lifts.
Move letter targets to where you tap

LocalType already learns where your finger lands on each letter, to make spelling correction better. With this on, each letter’s touch target also moves toward that spot, by up to about a third of a key, once it has a dozen taps to go on. The keys look the same. Forget learned words starts it over.

Suggestions and corrections offer British spellings, like colour, organise, centre, travelling and grey, where the keyboard would have offered the American ones. Nothing you type is changed: an American spelling you type stays, and words you’ve kept, added or given your own capitals keep your spelling. Words whose spelling depends on the meaning, like program, check or tyre, are left as they are. The typing log is off while this is on.

Adds Welsh, on the British QWERTY keys: hold a vowel, w or y for the to bach (â ŵ ŷ) and the other accents. Hold Space to switch; the space bar shows the language you’re typing. This is an early test: the word lists come from Welsh Wikipedia and haven’t been checked by a native speaker, so some suggestions and corrections will be off, and there is no next-word model yet, so suggestions come from the list and from what you type. Slurs are left out. Its words are learned apart from the other languages. Chime, the extra models, proofreading, swipe typing and the typing log stay English only.
